proofs.requirement: A suspended vibrating beam contains a fluid-filled channel; a cell-induced frequency shift is calibrated to buoyant mass relative to displaced fluid.

currentRoot.supportingExcerpt: A suspended microchannel resonator weighs a cell relative to the fluid it displaces using the shift in a vibrating beam's frequency. Buoyant mass equals cell volume multiplied by the difference between cell and fluid density. It is not simply diameter or dry mass. Repeatedly measuring the same cell estimates mass accumulation rate; Godin reversed the flow to reintroduce the same cell to the sensor (a dynamic trap) and Cermak used serial sensors along one channel. Stevens investigated drug-response associations in specified cancer models and leukaemia samples, rather than universal clinical prediction.

proofs.requirement: Outer-membrane permeabilization can release cytochrome c into cytosol; distinguish the release readout from intact-cell killing and clinical benefit.

currentRoot.supportingExcerpt: BH3 means BCL-2 homology 3. BAX and BAK can permeabilise the mitochondrial outer membrane, releasing cytochrome c from between the mitochondrial membranes into the cytosol. Priming concerns proximity to that threshold, not merely protein abundance. HRK-derived peptide preferentially probes BCL-XL, while BAD-derived peptide also challenges BCL-2 and BCL-W; overlapping patterns and concentrations matter. The assay peptide is not a vaccine-antigen recognition test.

currentRoot.supportingExcerpt: In a fictional dynamic-profiling experiment, cells pre-exposed to vehicle show 20 percent normalised depolarisation when given a peptide, and cells pre-exposed to the drug show 55 percent for the same peptide. The increase is 35 percentage points, not a 35 percent killed-cell fraction, a causal variant finding or a safe treatment. Values can exceed 100 percent in the potential-dye protocol, so the scale must not be read as a literal cell-death fraction.

currentRoot.supportingExcerpt: A cell line arises through subculture of an initial primary culture. Finite lines have limited proliferative capacity; continuous lines can proliferate for prolonged periods under suitable conditions. Continuous growth does not itself establish malignancy. Lines may attach to surfaces or grow in suspension. Their source, passage history, medium and density shape the selected population. Cancer-line strains can diverge genetically and in drug response, so a familiar name does not guarantee identical biology across laboratories.

currentRoot.supportingExcerpt: The useful trade-off is preserved biology against time and repeatability. A characterised PDX supports growth under whole-animal dosing, usually on a months-long establishment clock. Expanded organoids support repeated direct tumour-cell experiments and panels, often over weeks; conventional epithelial cultures usually lack immune cells, while Neal's specialised method retained them. A short-term fragment may preserve resident neighbours for a local-interaction question over days, but their function must be demonstrated. No preparation is universally more predictive because it is more complex.

proofs.requirement: Co-presence or a bulk response does not establish tumor recognition, cell-specific causality or clinical benefit.

currentRoot.supportingExcerpt: Co-culture studies interactions among defined populations. Dijkstra and colleagues combined autologous blood lymphocytes with tumour organoids from mismatch repair-deficient colorectal cancer and from non-small-cell lung cancer, with enrichment and later killing measurements as separate stages. Neal and colleagues retained native immune components using a specialised air-liquid-interface organoid method. Presence, activation, tumour recognition and killing require different observations; neither model label establishes universal patient prediction.

proofs.requirement: BH3-only proteins and anti-apoptotic survival proteins regulate the illustrated BAX/BAK outer-membrane permeabilization route.

currentRoot.supportingExcerpt: The BCL-2 family contains survival proteins, including BCL-2, BCL-XL and MCL-1; BH3-only stress mediators, including BIM, BID and PUMA; and pore-forming effectors BAX and BAK. In experimental cells, loss of both BAX and BAK blocked several mitochondrial apoptotic responses, rather than every possible form of death.

proofs.requirement: Cytosolic cytochrome c participates in apoptosome/caspase-9 activation; the sketch is simplified rather than a complete universal death pathway.

currentRoot.supportingExcerpt: Intrinsic apoptosis involves mitochondrial outer-membrane permeabilisation, cytochrome c release into the cytosol, apoptosome assembly and caspase-9 activation upstream of executioner caspases such as caspase-3 and caspase-7. Death-receptor signalling can activate caspase-8; BID cleavage links this route to mitochondria. Initiator and executioner roles differ.
